### Observed differences

- In the later window, A06 is repeated more often within the cases that contain it: mean occurrences rose from 0.85 to about 1.18 per case while participation stayed at about 25 in 100 cases, i.e. roughly 3.5 executions per containing case before versus about 4.6 after. [OCC006]
- A08 shows the same pattern: mean occurrences rose from 0.38 to 0.64 per case while participation moved only from 15 to 19 in 100 cases (about 2.5 versus about 3.4 executions per containing case). [OCC008]
- A06's outgoing transitions shifted toward the loop: in the earlier window its most common successor was A09 (about 53% of A06's outgoing transitions, versus 44% for A08); in the later window A08 is the most common successor (about 54% versus 45% for A09), on 170 versus 235 observed outgoing transitions. [DIR006]
- The return edge stayed near-deterministic (A08 led back to A06 in about 97% of its outgoing transitions before and 98% after), and A06 and A08 now appear together in 19 of 100 cases versus 15 before, essentially always as interleaved or repeated runs. [DIR008, REL047]
- Several activities sit at different event positions: A02 and A05 occur earlier in the case (A02 median position 1.0 to 0.33; A05 median 1.0 to 0.33), while A12 occurs later (median 0.75 to 1.0). [POS002, POS005, POS012]
- Some routing shares moved: A01 now sends about 55% of its outgoing transitions to A04 (up from 42%, away from A11 and A02); A07 sends about 63% to A10 (up from 33%, on only 15 versus 19 transitions); A11 shifted from A10 (80% to 33%) toward A03 and A01, but on only about 10 versus 9 transitions. [DIR001, DIR007, DIR011]
- Spacing around A10 changed in both directions: gaps from A10 to A06 and to A09 became longer (more pairs 3–5 positions apart), while gaps from A10 to A04 became shorter. [LAG057, LAG060, LAG055]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the repetition loop between A06 and A08 is executed more times per case that enters it. Cases containing A06 executed it about 3.5 times on average before versus about 4.6 after, and A08 about 2.5 versus about 3.4 times, while entry into the loop barely moved (A06 in about 25 of 100 cases in both windows; A08 from 15 to 19 in 100). The routing into the loop strengthened: A06's dominant successor flipped from A09 (about 53%) to A08 (about 54%), the return edge A08→A06 stayed near-deterministic, and the exit to A09 still occurs (about 45%), with A09's overall level similar (0.48 versus 0.54 occurrences per case). The magnitudes close consistently: per 200 cases, A06 gained about 65 occurrences, A08 about 53, and A06→A08 transitions about 52 — the signature of roughly 50 extra loop passes rather than more cases entering the loop. Limitations: A06 and A08 occur in only about a quarter and a fifth of cases, so these profiles rest on roughly 30–51 cases per window, and the evidence provides no screening baseline, so chance sampling cannot be fully excluded. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the case mix (proportionally more cases of a kind that repeats this loop) rather than a change in the loop's own behaviour; occurrence, routing and co-occurrence indicators cannot separate these. [OCC006, OCC008, DIR006, DIR008, REL047, OCC009]

Other differences: A02 and A05 now occur earlier in the case's event order and A12 later, which is a position-distribution change and does not by itself show that these activities were moved [POS002, POS005, POS012]; A01 routes to A04 more often (42% to 55% of its outgoing transitions) [DIR001]; A07→A10 rose to about 63% and A11's outgoing mix shifted from A10 toward A03 and A01, both resting on very few observed transitions [DIR007, DIR011]; gaps from A10 to A06 and A09 lengthened while gaps to A04 shortened [LAG057, LAG060, LAG055]. These differences are not part of the main hypothesis.
